content.title: About
content.content: Potato, home fries with vegetables is a dish made from diced or sliced potatoes fried until golden together with carrots, bell peppers, onions and sometimes green peas. It is popular as a side dish or a light main meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes are the fourth most produced food crop worldwide after rice, wheat and corn.
Home fries originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a quick way to make a hearty side from readily available ingredients.
Combining potatoes with vegetables boosts the content of vitamins C and A compared with plain potatoes.
The dish is often served with tartar sauce or sour cream, adding probiotics and calcium.
When fried correctly, potatoes retain most of their starch, making them a good energy source.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vegetables such as bell pepper and peas provide vitamin C, which supports immunity and iron absorption.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are an excellent source of potassium, helping to regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: The vegetables and potato skin supply fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains beta‑carotene
items.content: Orange vegetables like carrots are high in beta‑carotene, a precursor to vitamin A.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs in potatoes provide sustained energy and satiety.

items.title: High calorie content when fried
items.content: Using a lot of oil can make the dish calorie‑dense, which may be undesirable for weight management.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to potatoes or certain vegetables.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Cooking at very high temperatures can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound. Fry on medium heat.

items.title: Salt and sodium
items.content: Excessive salt adds sodium, which can affect blood pressure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a side to meat, fish or vegetarian plates. Garnish with fresh herbs, sour cream or a light yogurt sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet or oven to restore crispness.
